items.followUp: What happens to a Star Topology network if its central hub fails?

rubric.why: The AND output is 1 only when both inputs are 1, for either expression.
rubric.description: Gives the correct output sequence for both AND expressions.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark if both output columns have the sequence 0, 0, 0, 1.

rubric.why: Identical output columns prove the commutative law.
rubric.description: States the columns are identical and gives the required equality.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the conclusion that A · B = B · A.

modelAnswer: A B | A · B | B · A
A · B outputs: 0, 0, 0, 1; B · A outputs: 0, 0, 0, 1.
The output columns are identical; therefore, A · B = B · A.

items.followUp: What happens to a Star Topology network if its central hub fails?

rubric.why: Star Topology depends on a central device to connect its nodes.
rubric.description: Identifies the central hub or switch as the point whose failure causes the problem.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming the central hub or switch.

rubric.why: Failure of the central device can interrupt communication across the network.
rubric.description: States that failure of the central device can stop the entire network from working.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining the effect on the network.

modelAnswer: The major disadvantage of Star Topology is that if its central hub or switch fails, the entire network may stop working.
